title: Kepler Health - API playbook & credits pathway discovery
summary: Intro discovery to understand Kepler's time-to-first-token needs, hosting constraints (PHI considerations), and pilot sizing. Discussed Redwood hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private, free credits quickstart, security artifacts (SOC2, KMS), and proposed next steps for a 2-week pilot and light benchmark. Customer concerned about PHI, data residency, latency and cost tradeoffs.
action_items: Maya Singh -> Send tailored security pack (SOC2, ISO doc, KMS integration notes) by 2026-04-24
Ben Ortiz -> Share small benchmark checklist + sample prompt set and suggested model/quant config by 2026-04-24
Aisha Carter -> Provide 3 representative prompt examples and expected QPS by 2026-04-24
next_steps: Schedule 30m technical kickoff with Tom + Ben for pilot infra (suggest 2026-04-27)
Start 2-week hosted pilot using free credits, initial model suggestion M2-13B-quant for latency/cost tradeoff
Security review follow-up once pack received; discuss Dedicated/Private pricing if pilot shows PHI retention needs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Ben (Redwood); Aisha, Tom, Evelyn (Kepler)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery to map time-to-first-token needs and security constraints for PHI use cases. Discussed free credits pilot flow and when Dedicated/Private would be required.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, account exec on Redwood. Ben from our infra team is here too. You all mind doing quick intros?
00:12 Aisha: Yeah hi, I'm Aisha, Head of AI at Kepler. We run clinical summarization and decision support — so PHI is a thing. Tom is our platform person and Evelyn runs security.
00:22 Tom: Hey all. Focused on latency and how we can get a small pilot integrated into our infra.
00:28 Evelyn: Hi, security questions up front: encryption, KMS, audit logs and residency.
00:33 Ben: Great. Quick note on roles - I usually take the infra questions. Maya will handle procurement/credits and next steps.
00:40 Maya: Perfect. The goal today is to understand what 'time-to-first-token' looks like for you and the constraints so we can map you to hosted quickstart with credits vs Dedicated or Private.
01:00 Aisha: Our hypothesis — we want developers to iterate quickly via PLG flow but any POC that touches PHI may need to be on a private plane. So two parallel tracks maybe.
01:12 Maya: Totally. For most teams we recommend starting hosted with free credits to validate prompts and UX. If PHI storage or residency constraints arise, we can elevate to Dedicated or Private.
01:24 Tom: How fast is it to get something running with the SDK? We have a 1-week dev sprint ideally.
01:30 Ben: For a simple path — time-to-first-token is usually measured as: signup, API key, SDK install, minimal prompt test. With our SDK + sample repo it's often hours. With PLG credits we can provision tokens immediately; sample collections and Postman/curl examples are in the quickstart.
01:48 Tom: Hours sounds good. But in production we need latency < 200ms p99 for short prompts. Does that push us to Dedicated?
01:56 Ben: It depends on throughput. Hosted endpoints have multi-tenant optimizations and can hit low latencies for single requests; for predictable p99 at scale, Dedicated with reserved pools is usually the recommendation. We can also do caching/prefix caching on the SDK to reduce effective p99.
02:10 Evelyn: On the security side, what exactly is logged? We can't have PHI in analytics.
02:16 Maya: We have different data retention tiers; hosted API by default can be configured to not store request/response payloads for enterprise plans. We'll include the SOC2/ISO packet and KMS integration options in the security pack.
02:28 Evelyn: Is there a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) option? We use HSM-backed keys in our cloud provider.
02:34 Ben: Yes, BYOK via customer KMS is supported in Dedicated and Private. For hosted we have an optional envelope encryption flow depending on plan — we'll detail in the doc.
02:44 Aisha: Ok that helps. For pilot success criteria — we want: 1) integration in dev environment within 1 week, 2) sample throughput of 50 QPS sustained with mean latency < 250ms, 3) quality parity vs current smaller model.
03:00 Maya: Good clear criteria. We'll propose a 2-week hosted pilot using free credits focused on those goals, and a short bench to validate throughput. If PHI becomes a blocker we'll discuss Dedicated/Private pricing.
03:12 Tom: About costs: how transparent are per-token costs + tooling to optimize? We need to measure unit economics per customer.
03:20 Ben: Console gives token-level breakdown, per-route latency and cost. Also Optimize recommendations can suggest quantization and batching settings to reduce unit costs. We'll share a sample cost dashboard.
03:32 Aisha: Any caveats with open models vs Redwood-verified models? We care about reproducibility.
03:38 Ben: We maintain a catalog with verified performance profiles per model. For pilot we'll recommend a mid-sized quantized model to balance latency/cost, and can run A/B with a higher-quality variant if you want.
03:48 Evelyn: On compliance, do you run yearly pen tests and provide evidence?
03:52 Maya: Yes, pen test summary and SOC2 report are in the security pack. For Dedicated/Private we can offer additional attestation if needed.
04:00 Tom: Integration path — we prefer server-side calls from our VPC. Is there a VPC peering or Private option?
04:06 Ben: For VPC you'd look at Private or Redwood Private. We have a private control plane and can do customer-managed networking for on-prem or VPC deployments. Dedicated can also be deployed in a customer's cloud region in some cases.
04:18 Aisha: Could you outline recommended pilot architecture? Hosted first — what's the flow for PHI minimization while prototyping?
04:24 Ben: Typical approach: stub PHI with synthetic data in dev for model tuning, use hosted with data retention disabled and endpoint-level masking. If performance and security checks pass, promote to Dedicated/Private with BYOK for production.
04:38 Maya: I shared earlier a short checklist in the invite — Ben will send a bench checklist and sample prompt set. I'll send credits redemption instructions and a tailored security pack.
04:48 Tom: Onboarding docs — do you have a quickstart repo? We prefer Terraform + k8s examples.
04:52 Ben: Yes, sample repo includes SDK examples, Postman, Terraform for infra hooks, and a quick k8s sidecar example for inference routing. We'll point you to the repo link in the follow-up.
05:02 Aisha: We may also want a short demo for execs showing latency and cost tradeoffs — maybe a 15-min session after the pilot starts.
05:08 Maya: Sure, we can do an exec check-in.
05:10 Evelyn: A quick question — do you support audit logs per token/request that we can ship to our SIEM?
05:14 Ben: Yes — audit logs can be forwarded; for Hosted we export only metadata unless you opt-in. For Dedicated/Private we can ship full payload logs into your logging bucket if policy allows.
05:26 Tom: Are there any gotchas for KV cache behavior? We use a lot of LLM caching for clinical templates.
05:30 Ben: We have KV cache and prefix caching; sometimes the transcriptions call it KV 'cash' in older docs, ha, but the behavior is predictable: you keep key-value state per session and it reduces token compute significantly. We'll document recommended eviction/TTL for clinical workloads.
05:44 Aisha: Ok. On parties — who will own the pilot on Redwood's side?
05:47 Maya: I'll be your AE contact; Ben will be the SE. I'll handle credits and contract.
05:52 Maya: (to Ben) Any recommended model for initial test?
05:55 Ben: For latency/cost balance start with M2-13B-quant-ish variant, then expand to M2-70B for quality checks if needed. Use continuous batching at the runtime level to keep latency tight.
06:08 Aisha: Good. Any integration friction with our existing auth (we use SSO + SAML)?
06:12 Maya: We support SSO/SAML and RBAC for console access. We'll include steps for SAML setup in the security pack.
06:20 Evelyn: Is there a formal escalation for incident response? We need a dedicated contact if production affects clinical flows.
06:25 Maya: Yes, enterprise support tiers include a named response contact and runbook mapping. We'll include SLA artifacts and support tiers.
06:34 Tom: Ok can you affirm the pilot won't cost us beyond the free credits initially? We need to budget for eventual Dedicated.
06:40 Maya: The hosted pilot will be covered by credits. If you exceed credits we'll notify and pause; upgrade to Dedicated is a separate contract.
06:46 Aisha: Great. Sounds like a path: hosted pilot (free credits) -> verify latency/quality -> if PHI blocking, move to Dedicated/Private with BYOK.
06:56 Maya: Exactly. I'll send an email recap after this with the docs and meeting links.
07:02 Ben: I'll add the bench checklist: sample prompts, expected QPS, p99 goals, and a small snippet to measure p99 locally.
07:10 Aisha: We'll gather sample prompts and provide by Friday.
07:14 Tom: Can we book the technical kickoff for Monday afternoon?
07:18 Maya: I'll propose Monday 2026-04-27 15:00 UTC in the follow-up.
07:24 Evelyn: Thanks all.
07:26 Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the security pack, bench checklist, repo links and credit redemption.
07:32 End.
